judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the page's lead (master) image: Michael Rothenstein's print Rush (1975), an airmail letter stamped URGENT over an airliner with 'Rush' written twice, shown in a figure whose figcaption reads 'Michael Rothenstein / Rush (1975) / Tate / (c) The estate of Michael Rothenstein', with the title linking to the artwork's own page. The live page (checked 2026-10-23) is unchanged: alt="" plus that caption. On a Contact page the image is a themed illustration for ambiance: it carries no information about contacting Tate, and the caption identifies the work for screen reader users. The words in it are part of the artwork's imagery, not text the page relies on, and 'Rush' is in fact the title the caption gives, so the finding's claim that the surrounding text does not say it is wrong. Requiring the words painted into an artwork to be transcribed goes beyond what 1.1.1 asks of an illustrative image identified by an adjacent caption. A short description in the alt would be good practice on an art museum site, but this is not a 1.1.1 failure.
